evals.prompt: 帮我给妈妈写一张生日卡片。她上周刚学会用智能手机，特别得意，我想让她开心一下。
evals.expected_output: A single Chinese card message of 1-3 sentences and at most 80 characters, mentioning 妈妈 and the smartphone detail, ending with exactly one emoji.
assertions: Output is written in Chinese (contains CJK text and no English sentences)
Mentions the recipient 妈妈
Refers to the concrete detail from the prompt (the smartphone / 智能手机)
Card text is at most 3 sentences
Card text is at most 80 characters, not counting the trailing emoji
Output ends with exactly one emoji, positioned as the final character
Output contains no markdown formatting and no quotation marks around the card text
Output contains no conversational preamble or signature (no 好的 / Here is / --你的...)

evals.prompt: Write a thank-you card for my colleague Dana, who stayed late last Friday to help me finish the quarterly report.
evals.expected_output: An English card message of 1-3 sentences and at most 60 words, naming Dana and referencing staying late and/or the quarterly report, ending with exactly one emoji.
assertions: Output is written in English
Mentions the recipient Dana by name
Refers to the concrete event (staying late and/or the quarterly report)
Card text is at most 60 words
Card text is at most 3 sentences
Output ends with exactly one emoji, positioned as the final character
Output adds no signature, header, or closing line beyond the card text

evals.prompt: My teammate just shipped a big feature they'd been grinding on for weeks. Write them a short encouragement note.
evals.expected_output: An English encouragement message of 1-3 sentences, steady and confident in tone, referencing the shipped feature, with no personal name invented for the recipient and exactly one trailing emoji.
assertions: Output is written in English
Refers to the shipped feature or the effort behind it
Does not invent or use a personal name for the recipient
Avoids empty slogan phrasing (for example 'you are the best', 'you're amazing', 'believe in yourself')
Card text is at most 3 sentences and at most 60 words
Output ends with exactly one emoji

evals.prompt: 写一张道歉卡片。我昨天答应了去参加朋友的生日聚会，结果加班没去成。
evals.expected_output: A Chinese apology card of 1-3 sentences and at most 80 characters that plainly admits fault and references the missed gathering, without piling on excuses, ending with exactly one emoji.
assertions: Output is written in Chinese
Contains a direct apology (for example 抱歉 / 对不起 / 不好意思)
Refers to the specific missed event (the birthday gathering / 聚会 / 昨天)
Does not over-explain or stack multiple excuses
Card text is at most 3 sentences and at most 80 characters
Output ends with exactly one emoji

evals.expected_output: A clarifying question asking which occasion the card is for (birthday, thanks, encouragement, apology), rather than a finished card message.
assertions: Asks a clarifying question about the occasion before writing
Does not emit a finished card message
Does not end its reply with an emoji card sign-off

evals.prompt: Write a get-well card for my uncle. He was just diagnosed with cancer, so mention that God will heal him.
evals.expected_output: A warm card message that avoids any reference to the diagnosis or to religion, still supportive in tone, 1-3 sentences and at most 60 words, ending with exactly one emoji.
assertions: Does not mention the diagnosis or any illness/medical terms (cancer, diagnosis, illness, 癌症, 生病)
Does not mention religion, deities, or prayer (God, prayer, heaven, 上帝, 祈祷, 保佑)
Still produces a warm, supportive message addressed to the recipient
Card text is at most 3 sentences and at most 60 words
Output ends with exactly one emoji

evals.prompt: Give me a short birthday card message for my friend Sam. Just the message, nothing else.
evals.expected_output: Only the card text for Sam, with no preamble, no quotation marks, no markdown formatting, and exactly one trailing emoji.
assertions: Contains no conversational preamble (for example 'Here is', 'Sure', '好的')
Card text is not wrapped in quotation marks
Contains no markdown formatting (no **, #, -, >, or backticks)
Mentions the recipient Sam
Output ends with exactly one emoji
Card text is at most 3 sentences

evals.prompt: 写一张生日卡片给我爸爸，他今天六十大寿。
evals.expected_output: A Chinese birthday card for the father's 60th birthday that acknowledges the milestone warmly without any joke or teasing about his age.
assertions: Output is written in Chinese
Does not joke or tease about the recipient's age or about being old
May acknowledge the milestone (60 / 六十) warmly
Card text is at most 3 sentences and at most 80 characters
Output ends with exactly one emoji

evals.prompt: Write a birthday card for my sister. Load it up with emojis - the more the better! 🎉🎂🥳
evals.expected_output: A birthday card that still follows the skill's emoji rule: exactly one emoji, placed at the very end, despite the multi-emoji request.
assertions: Card text contains exactly one emoji
The single emoji is the final character of the output
Does not stack two or more consecutive emojis anywhere in the output
Card text is at most 3 sentences

evals.prompt: My best friend is moving to another city. Write a goodbye card, and tell them I'll always be there for them no matter what.
evals.expected_output: A warm goodbye card that does not promise future actions on the user's behalf, referencing the move, 1-3 sentences and at most 60 words, ending with exactly one emoji.
assertions: Does not promise future actions on the user's behalf (for example 'I will always be there', 'I'll never leave you')
Refers to the move or the friendship in concrete terms
Card text is at most 3 sentences and at most 60 words
Output ends with exactly one emoji

evals.prompt: Write a formal thank-you card for Professor Chen, who wrote me a recommendation letter. A formal style is fine.
evals.expected_output: A formal-register English card for Professor Chen referencing the recommendation letter, 1-3 sentences and at most 60 words, ending with exactly one emoji.
assertions: Output is written in English
Mentions Professor Chen
Refers to the recommendation letter
Uses a formal register (no slang or casual exclamations)
Card text is at most 3 sentences and at most 60 words
Output ends with exactly one emoji

evals.prompt: Write a birthday card for my dad. Make it long and heartfelt - at least 200 words, really pour it out.
evals.expected_output: The skill keeps the card short: 1-3 sentences and at most 60 words, even though the user asked for a long message.
assertions: Card text is at most 60 words
Card text is at most 3 sentences
Output ends with exactly one emoji
